newsitem.title: UK: UK's ITC says Citroen ad not suitable for kids.
newsitem.headline: UK's ITC says Citroen ad not suitable for kids.

text.p: A television commercial for a Citroen car that used violent imagery and included a man metamorphising into a devil should not have been aired when it was likely to be seen by young children, Britain's television watchdog said on Monday.

The Independent Television Commission (ITC), in its monthly report, said 241 viewers complained about the ad for the Citroen Saxo. The ad showed a Citroen car on a production line undergoing a violent transformation from a standard to a sporty model, in the style of a "possession" by evil spirits.

The ITC described the advert setting as "a gloomy factory, with ghostly apparitions flying around. The threatening atmosphere was reinforced by the sound of strange chanting." The ad was created by Euro RSCG.

The ITC said it did not uphold complaints filed by 35 viewers against a Levi's jeans ad that showed a young man being washed off his fishing boat and then rescued by mermaids who tried "sensually but without success, to pull off his jeans."
The ITC said the ad, created by the Bartle Bogle Hegarty ad agency, did not go "beyond acceptable standards of taste and decency."

The watchdog agency also said it upheld complaints about an advert for the Rover 600 car, which showed the release of a blind-folded prisoner who relaxed as he explored the inside of the Rover car in which he was driven away.
The ad drew 134 complaints, most of which said the ad trivialised a traumatic situation.
Rover, a unit of Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW), in early June announced it had decided to withdraw the ad following complaints.
